sections.description: Walks through the patient's demographics, pregnancy status, presenting symptoms, bedside assessment, and immediate supportive care to frame the clinical problem before imaging.
subtopics: Patient profile: nulliparous woman in her 40s, BMI 33, singleton pregnancy at 21 weeks’ gestation; prior aneuploidy screening and fetal morphology normal
Symptoms: acute left upper quadrant and pelvic pain with dyspnoea; pain scoring and temporal evolution
Vital signs and cardiopulmonary assessment: normal oxygen saturation and ECG; attribution of dyspnoea to mechanical restriction rather than cardiopulmonary disease
Abdominal and pelvic examination: enlarged abdomen for gestational age; palpable 18 cm taut-elastic mass in left upper quadrant; bimanual exam with fixed, hard 9 cm mass bulging posterior fornix
Initial symptom control: pregnancy-safe analgesia (paracetamol) and semi-orthostatic positioning to relieve diaphragmatic compression; baseline fetal well-being assessment

Laboratory context: iron-deficiency anaemia; physiologic leukocytosis and mildly elevated CRP in pregnancy; evaluation of low-grade fever and identification of Klebsiella pneumoniae UTI with implications for antibiotic selection

sections.section_title: Pregnancy-Safe Diagnostics and Differential Diagnosis of Large Abdominal Masses
sections.description: Explains the imaging and laboratory workup feasible in pregnancy, interprets the specific sonographic and MRI findings, and develops the differential between adnexal and uterine etiologies.
subtopics: Imaging strategy in pregnancy: role and safety of ultrasound with color Doppler as first line; indications for non-contrast MRI after first trimester; avoidance of gadolinium and preference for 1.5-T scanners

Ultrasound findings: two large unilocular cystic masses with peripheral vascularisation; upper lesion spanning left subphrenic space to uterine fundus; lower lesion in pouch of Douglas adherent to a posterior intramural–subserosal myoma
Serum tumour markers: limitations and physiology of CA-125 in pregnancy; normal CA 19-9, CA 15-3, CEA, β2-microglobulin, LDH; value of serial CA-125 trend (mild rise) over single measurements

MRI characteristics: thick-walled cysts with inhomogeneous T1/T2 fat-saturated fluid, focal hyperintense components, hypertrophied vessels; caudal mass continuity with uterine tissue; absence of adenopathy
Pathophysiology refreshers: decidualised endometrioma features in pregnancy; cystic/ischemic degeneration in leiomyomas; torsion risks in pedunculated subserosal fibroids

Structured differential diagnosis: decidualised endometriomas, pedunculated/degenerating uterine leiomyomas, benign ovarian cysts/paraovarian cysts, ovarian neoplasm; malignancy red flags in pregnancy

Diagnostic synthesis in this case: mild CA-125 elevation nudging toward endometrioma for the upper cyst vs anatomic continuity pointing to myomatous origin for the caudal lesion; dyspnoea attributed to mass effect

sections.section_title: Operative Indications, Planning, and Technique in Mid-Trimester Myomectomy
sections.description: Details why and how the team moved from conservative observation to surgery, balancing maternal–fetal risks, and describes the intraoperative findings and selective myomectomy approach.
subtopics: Indications to operate in pregnancy: refractory pain and restrictive dyspnoea, risk of torsion/rupture/infection, diagnostic uncertainty with oncologic concern, and anticipated uterine/mass growth limiting space
Timing and route: rationale for second-trimester intervention; factors favoring laparotomy over laparoscopy (mass size, number, intramural location, gestational age, distorted anatomy)
Preoperative planning and consent: multidisciplinary discussion; documentation of fetal heart rate before, during, and after surgery; perioperative obstetric preparedness

Intraoperative steps and findings: peritoneal fluid sampling; confirmation of fetal viability; identification of a twisted, highly vascular, leaking pedunculated cystic leiomyoma; pedicle control with double clamp, resection, and uterine bed closure with absorbable suture
Selective myomectomy decision-making: leaving the fixed caudal intramural–subserosal myoma in situ to minimize hemorrhage, uterine irritability, and pregnancy loss risk
Adjunctive measures: progesterone prophylaxis perioperatively and during follow-up; culture-directed antibiotics for concurrent UTI; strategies to minimize operative time and uterine manipulation
Pregnancy-specific risk mitigation: hemodynamic control, prevention of preterm contractions, and careful hemostasis in a hypervascular uterus

sections.section_title: Postoperative Care, Ongoing Obstetric Management, and Delivery
sections.description: Covers maternal recovery, hematologic optimization, fetal surveillance, pathology interpretation, delivery planning in the presence of a residual obstructive myoma, and postnatal course.
subtopics: Hematologic management: recognition of postoperative anaemia; indications for IV iron (ferric carboxymaltose) and packed RBC transfusion; reassessment of hemoglobin response
Pathology and fluid analysis: benign leiomyoma with ischemic necrosis near twisted pedicle; negative peritoneal cytology/culture
Obstetric follow-up: serial ultrasounds every 3 weeks for fetal growth (noting high percentile) and amniotic fluid; continuation of progesterone regimen
Delivery planning with residual myoma: assessing risk of labor obstruction; rationale for elective cesarean at 37 weeks on existing midline scar to reduce rupture risk
Outcomes: uncomplicated maternal recovery; healthy neonate; postpartum partial regression of the residual pelvic myoma and absence of symptoms
Long-term considerations: shared decision to defer further surgery; counseling on the natural history of postpartum fibroid regression and future reproductive plans

sections.section_title: Key Teaching Points and Evidence-Guided Practice
sections.description: Synthesizes the clinical lessons, provides practical algorithms, and links decisions to current evidence to guide evaluation and management of atypical abdominal masses in pregnancy.
subtopics: Structured evaluation algorithm: thorough history, bimanual and abdominal exam, first-line ultrasound with Doppler, selective non-contrast MRI, and judicious use of tumour markers with serial trends
Differentiating fibroids from adnexal masses: imaging pearls (continuity with myometrium, vascular patterns, degeneration signs) and the pitfall of fibroids mimicking ovarian cysts
Interpreting CA-125 in pregnancy: expected trimester-related changes; benign causes of elevation; when values and imaging warrant escalation for malignancy workup

When to operate: maternal–fetal indications (pain, dyspnoea, torsion/rupture/infection risk, rapid growth, diagnostic uncertainty); choosing laparoscopy vs laparotomy based on size, location, and gestational age
Operative pearls in pregnancy: minimize uterine manipulation and operative time; pedicle control and meticulous hemostasis; selective myomectomy to preserve pregnancy
Fetal monitoring standards for non-obstetric surgery: document heart rate before, intermittently during, and after the procedure
Delivery planning with fibroids: anticipate malpresentation/obstruction; criteria for cesarean vs trial of labor; evidence on myomectomy at cesarean and impacts on operative time and hospitalization
Natural history of fibroids: growth acceleration early in pregnancy and regression postpartum; counseling based on size dynamics to avoid overtreatment
Imaging safety principles: avoid gadolinium in pregnancy unless absolutely necessary; prefer non-contrast MRI after first trimester at 1.5 T
